title: The proper closed-complement square and mixed open restriction
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $W,Y,\overline Y$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $r:W\to\overline Y$ be proper, let $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, and let $c:Z\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ be a closed immersion with $|c(Z)|=|\overline Y|\setminus|i(Y)|$ [def-weil-proper-morphism; def-weil-open-immersion; def-weil-closed-immersion]. All maps are over $k$. Form $U=W\times_{\overline Y}Y$ and $T=W\times_{\overline Y}Z$, with projections $j:U\to W$, $a:T\to W$, and $r_Z:T\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $U,Z,T$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, $a$ is a closed immersion, $r_Z$ is proper, and $|a(T)|=|W|\setminus|j(U)|$. For every commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], using ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories and coefficient-compatible total derived pullback [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and exact termwise open extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek], one has
$$a^*j_!B\simeq0\quad\text{in }D(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$$
for every $B\in D(U_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$. Neither $Z$ nor $T$ is required to be reduced.

proof.text: Base-change i along r: the first projection j is an open immersion and quasi-compact. Base-change c along r: the first projection a is a closed immersion. Base-change r along c: the second projection r_Z is proper. These are the Mathlib scheme pullback permanence instances.

A closed immersion is proper, hence separated and finite type. Thus c followed by the structure map of Ybar is separated and finite type, and Over.w c identifies this composite with the structure map of Z. The open immersion j is separated and locally of finite type, and is quasi-compact by step 1. Compose j with the structure map of W to obtain the asserted properties of U. Likewise compose the closed immersion a with the structure map of W for T. These instances use separated, locally finite-type and quasi-compact composition.

Apply Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.range_fst to both pullbacks. Their ranges are r inverse-image of range(c) and range(i). Rewrite range(c) by the given complement equality; inverse image commutes with complement. This proves complementarity without any reducedness assumption or field-point factorization.

proof.text: For every integer n, exactness of open extension identifies H^n(j_!B) with j_!H^n(B). Pull this isomorphism back along a and apply the existing disjoint-image module vanishing theorem to H^n(B), using complementarity from step 3. Thus F kills every homology object of j_!B. Functor.isZero_mapDerivedCategory_obj (exact derived functors commute with homology and homology detects zero) makes D(F)(j_!B) zero. Transport this zero object along the comparison from step 4. No boundedness is used.

Source: main-20261015 det-sf-comp-composition-interchange proof (3), which says r^{-1}(Ybar∖Y)=W∖Xbar and that j'_!A vanishes there; the item states exactly this, generalized to any condensed ring Λ, unbounded B and a closed Z that need not be reduced, and its parent lem-sfb-proper-open-boundary-zero uses it in its step 1. Step 1: open-immersion, quasi-compact and proper/closed-immersion base change; the swapped fibre-product factors are identified by the uniqueness in def-pc-fibre-product. Step 2: separated finite type through permanence (c)/(e) and finite-type composition (1). Step 3: the open image comes from lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product. For the reverse inclusion of the closed image, the residue-field point of w factors through Z by field-point-factors-through-closed-immersion, which needs only that the image point lies in c(Z), with no reducedness; the fibre-product property then lifts it to T. So there is no E3 'image inside implies factors' error. Step 4: j_! is termwise (sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek) and a^* is exact (det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main), so La^* agrees with the termwise functor (def-sfb-left-derived-exact) under the hypotheses of sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, which is a stmt_dep. Step 5: disjoint-image module vanishing applied termwise, then the zero complex is zero. Edge cases checked: U, Z, W empty; Λ=0; nonreduced Z=Spec k[t]/(t^2) with Y=D(t). Accepted tool_uses: field-point factorization, module pullback exactness, exact-functor derived comparison, disjoint vanishing and finite-type permanence.
